chosen_by: Claude, 2026-10-25, for Jeff to check (docs/plans/v2-stereoisomers.md, bar A.2)
how: Written by reading each structure, before any enumerator was run on it; never generated. For each compound: what the panel should list (the count after duplicates are merged, or 'counted' / 'too-many' / 'no-elements'), how many enantiomer pairs, achiral and meso stereoisomers it lists, how many are marked as matching the drawing (none when the drawing defines no stereo), and which notes it shows. 'exist' is the chemist's count where it differs from what the panel can list. 'meso' follows IUPAC: an achiral stereoisomer in a set that also has chiral ones. A test compares the generated tests/fixtures/stereoisomers_expected.json with this file.

compounds.name: 2,3-dibromobutane
compounds.why: (R,R), (S,S) and the meso (R,S)

compounds.name: tartaric acid
compounds.why: L-, D- and meso-tartaric acid; PubChem's record is L

compounds.name: L-threonine, one centre undefined
compounds.why: the defined centre fits two of the four

compounds.name: ephedrine
compounds.why: ephedrine and pseudoephedrine, each a pair

compounds.name: menthol
compounds.why: three centres, no symmetry; PubChem's menthol record has no stereo

compounds.name: 2,3,4-pentanetriol
compounds.why: (2R,4R)/(2S,4S) pair, where C3 is not a stereocentre; two meso forms, C3 r and s (pseudo-asymmetric)

compounds.name: 1,2-dimethylcyclohexane
compounds.why: cis is meso; trans is a pair

compounds.name: 1,3-dimethylcyclohexane
compounds.why: cis is meso; trans is a pair

compounds.name: 1,4-dimethylcyclohexane
compounds.why: cis and trans, both achiral; not meso, since the set has no chiral member

compounds.name: trans-decalin
compounds.why: cis- and trans-decalin, both achiral; PubChem's record (decalin) has no stereo

compounds.name: myo-inositol
compounds.why: the nine inositols: seven achiral (cis, epi, allo, myo, muco, neo, scyllo) and the D/L-chiro pair; PubChem's record has no stereo

compounds.name: 2,4-hexadiene
compounds.why: (E,E), (Z,Z), and (E,Z) which is the same as (Z,E)

compounds.name: methyl phenyl sulfoxide
compounds.why: a stereocentre at sulfur

compounds.name: 1,2-dimethylaziridine
compounds.why: the ring nitrogen inverts slowly, so cis and trans are each a pair. Revised 2026-10-25: first judged 2, on the wrong belief that InChI ignores this nitrogen

compounds.name: Troger's base
compounds.why: its chirality is in two bridgehead nitrogens, which RDKit does not treat as stereo elements, so there is no button (a known limit). Revised 2026-10-25: first judged as listed with a note

compounds.name: 2,3-pentadiene
compounds.why: an allene: chiral by its axis, which RDKit does not treat as a stereo element, so there is no button. The panel still opens, to say RDKit can't judge it (revised 2026-10-25)

compounds.name: trans-cyclooctene
compounds.why: E and Z; the E form is chiral (planar chirality), which RDKit cannot judge, so neither may be called achiral

compounds.name: camphor
compounds.why: two bridgeheads give four combinations, but the bridge forces them together: only the (1R,4R)/(1S,4S) pair exists

compounds.name: cocaine
compounds.why: four carbon centres, two of them bridgeheads tied together by the bridge, so 8 exist. Revised 2026-10-25: a nitrogen note was dropped, since RDKit does not vary the bridgehead nitrogen

compounds.name: cholesterol
compounds.why: eight centres, no symmetry: 2⁸, too many to draw

compounds.name: erythromycin
compounds.why: more than eight stereo elements

compounds.name: 1,1'-bi-2-naphthol
compounds.why: BINOL: chiral by its biaryl axis only, invisible to RDKit. The panel still opens, to say RDKit can't judge it (revised 2026-10-25)

compounds.name: (R)-2-butanol, racemic
compounds.why: a racemic drawing (chiral flag 0) matches both enantiomers

compounds.name: joined: 2,3-pentadiene + (R)-2-butanol
compounds.why: made by the generator to put an allene beside a stereocentre; the counts depend on where it joins, so only the note is judged, and nothing may be called achiral

compounds.name: joined: 1,1'-bi-2-naphthol + (R)-2-butanol
compounds.why: made by the generator to put a biaryl axis beside a stereocentre; only the note is judged, and nothing may be called achiral

compounds.name: hepta-2,5-dien-4-ol
compounds.why: (E,E) and (Z,Z) are achiral, C4 then not being a stereocentre; in (E,Z) C4 is one, so (E,Z) is a pair. Meso by IUPAC's rule, since the set has chiral members

compounds.name: 2,4-pentanediol
compounds.why: (R,R)/(S,S) and the meso (R,S)

compounds.name: 3-ethylidenepentane-2,4-diol
compounds.why: made by the generator from 2,4-pentanediol. (R,R)/(S,S), where the double bond is not stereogenic (its two sides are the same), and the two (R,S) forms, where it is: those two are each other's mirror image

compounds.name: L-threonine, wedge and hash with H drawn
compounds.why: threonine as students wedge it; the same answer as L-threonine

compounds.name: (R)-2-butanol, wedge and hash with H drawn
cyclooctatetraene
compounds.why: four ring double bonds, each E or Z, give six patterns around the ring: all Z, one E, two E side by side, two E opposite, three E, all E. Only all-Z exists in practice; double bonds in a ring, so nothing is called achiral. PubChem's record is all-Z. Added after the review found the panel failed on it, so judged after a probe, not blind

compounds.name: 2,3-dibromobutane, the meso form
compounds.why: made by the generator: the meso (R,S) form drawn with wedges, the third of (R,R), (S,S) and meso

compounds.name: estradiol
compounds.why: five stereocentres (C8, C9, C13, C14, C17) and no symmetry: 2^5, all chiral; fused rings, not bridged. Added in review round 2 for a crowded picture

compounds.name: limonene
compounds.why: one stereocentre (C4); the ring double bond is in a six-membered ring; PubChem's limonene record has no stereo

compounds.name: (3E)-3-penten-2-ol
compounds.why: a centre and an E/Z double bond: (R,E)/(S,E) and (R,Z)/(S,Z); the record fixes E only, so both E forms match

compounds.name: joined: 1,1'-bi-2-naphthol + (R)-2-butanol, axis wedged
compounds.why: made by the generator: the joined drawing with a wedge at the biaryl axis. The axis is not varied, so the list is the centre's two forms, as unwedged; the R form matches
